qt: to the Commission Mathilde Androuët (PfE) Subject:

A European Court of Auditors report says that imports of Russian gas went from 153 billion cubic metres (bcm) to 38 bcm between 2021 and 2024, while imports of Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) increased by 67 %1. This shift was accompanied by a larger share of the EU’s supplies coming from the US and Norway2. Regulation (EU) 2026/261 now governs the phasing out of Russian gas and strengthens the monitoring of energy dependencies. In France, Russian gas imports reached 7.4 bcm in 2024, almost entirely in the form of LNG3 1.

Has the Commission assessed, for each Member State, the concentration risks associated with LNG supplies, particularly when sourced from the US, and the consequences of price and import cost volatility for households and industry?
Will it publish, under Regulation (EU) 2026/261, an assessment per Member State of the origin, volumes, costs and actual diversification of supplies, subject to trade secrets?

How will it ensure, in accordance with Article 194(2) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, respect for national energy choices and technological neutrality, so that France can limit its energy dependence by prioritising nuclear, hydropower and its dispatchable generation capacity?
European Court of Auditors, special report 21/2026, paragraphs 60-61. ibid, paragraph 62. ibid., Annex VI.
